resources.string: Menu or race?\nThe game says which. While you drive you get the racing layout: steering buttons, pedals, gears and the rest. In the menus, and whenever a menu opens over a race, the port shows no buttons at all: the menus take a touch themselves, the phone\'s own back is Escape, and the keyboard comes up by itself. There is nothing to switch by hand.

How do the menus work?\nTouch them. Where you put a finger is where the game’s pointer goes, so a tap presses the item under it and a slider follows the finger that drags it. The phone\'s back button or gesture is Escape, and when the game asks for a name the phone\'s keyboard opens on its own; with the keyboard open, back closes it.

What does size change?\nButton size scales the default controls. In Edit positions & sizes, drag a control and move the Button slider to resize it; a control answers to touches exactly where it is drawn, and percentages are relative to the default control. Changes save automatically. The editor shows a grid; with Snap to grid on, a dragged control lands on it.
Edges and vertical position\nDistance from edges moves default controls inward. System cutouts are respected. Manually placed controls keep their saved positions.

Opacity and auto-hide\nOpacity sets normal visibility. Auto-hide starts after all fingers lift, after a delay of 1–30 seconds. Hidden buttons still respond on the first touch and become visible again. Holding a control prevents hiding. A press on player 1\'s pad hides the controls at once; the next touch brings them back. Player 2\'s pad leaves them alone, so one player can drive on the screen while the other plays on a pad.

Vibration\nThe game\'s Force Feedback effects reach the phone and Gamepad 1. The game drives only one force-feedback device, so Gamepad 2 never vibrates. Phone vibration is switched on or off in Controls → Touch. Gamepad vibration is off until you switch it on in Controls → Gamepads; its strength is set in the game itself: Options → Controllers → Force Feedback. Effects come from the game, never from button taps.

Gamepads\nThe game always sees two gamepads: Gamepad 1 is player 1 together with the touch controls, Gamepad 2 is player 2. In Controls → Gamepads pick which pad is which by pressing a button on it and set what each button does, then press Gamepad ON once: it writes matching controls into the game\'s settings and backs up the old file. The left stick steers, the triggers accelerate and brake. A pad has two sets of buttons, as the touch controls have two layouts: the racing one you set up here, and a fixed one for the menus and replays, where Cross / A confirms, Circle / B goes back and the D-pad moves the selection. To play on a keyboard, press Default in game instead.
Lights and recovery\n☼ sends L. ↻ sends R to return to the track. The keys can be changed in Controls → Touch → Keys.

Screen and game data\nLandscape locks the game horizontally; Auto permits rotation. FPS cap limits frame rate; a lower value can reduce work per second. Game data manages imports and shows which data set is active. Play is enabled when a data set is ready.
